title: Add 'root-cause' default to defaults.toml
summary: Append one [[default]] entry, id "root-cause", to defaults.toml, sourced to "BRIEF.md 2026-10-13: Root causes". Its statement covers fixing at the origin, naming out-of-scope causes with a proposed fix, describing the root cause in the fix, and how this relates to 'small'. No BRIEF.md edit and no code change.

defaults_applied.how: One entry in one governance file, with no code or doc changes beyond it.
The statement is plain enough for an outside reader to follow without context.
The source field cites the BRIEF.md addendum.
The existing parse test guards the file's validity. The rule itself is prose, delivered to briefs by the defaults renderer.
cargo test and clippy must still pass.
The verifier runs cargo test to confirm the file parses.
The id, source and statement points were all given, and the file layout was recovered from the repository.

assumptions: applies_to is ["*"], because failure reports can concern code, tests, docs, config or builds.
The entry is appended at the end of the file and the file's version stays 1, since entries are added without changing the schema.
The statement is one string of a few sentences, in the style of the other entries, though longer.
docs/decisions.md line 634 ('eleven defaults') is a historical decision record and is left alone.

acceptance_criteria.text: defaults.toml has exactly one new [[default]] entry with id = "root-cause", placed after the existing entries, with the same four keys (id, statement, applies_to, source) as the others.
The source field cites the BRIEF.md addendum by name, e.g. "BRIEF.md 2026-10-13: Root causes".
The statement says: when a request reports a failure, find where the fault originates and fix it there, not the symptom or the one instance that surfaced.
The statement says: when the root cause lies outside the request's scope, name it and propose the fix instead of silently working around it.
The statement says: a fix's description names the root cause and why the change addresses it, so the verifier can check it.
The statement says how it relates to 'small': the root-cause fix is the one focused change, and an out-of-scope cause is reported, not fixed.
BRIEF.md and the existing eleven defaults entries are unchanged, and the version value stays 1 unless the change gives a reason to bump it.

Run `cargo test -p athena-data`: repository_defaults_parse passes, so the file parses with no duplicate ids. Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy`: both pass, since several crates embed defaults.toml with include_str!.

out_of_scope: Changing prompts, briefs or code so the verifier checks root-cause descriptions mechanically
Updating the historical 'eleven defaults' line in docs/decisions.md
departures: This is a one-entry data edit with a ready-made parse test, so cost and time are below the reference. Only the wording of the statement is open to judgment.
